posts.content_md:
Hello guys,

 i am trying to reconstruct a reflection hologram using near IR diode laser of 763nm precisely. Hologram was recorded at 633nm. I want to predict the reconstruction angle and probing angle with 763nm, due to wavelength shift. i am recording on a silver halide layers. i ignored considering shrinkage due to processing but just applying Snell's laws and Bragg's law i want to predict the angle of reconstruction and probing angle with 763nm.( i am not considering magnification of image depending on position of the source or observer). I derived an equation for transmission grating but for reflection hologram, completely baffled with sign conventions of ray. i am taking ray traveling from left to right normal to the surface of the silver halide plate as reference and also angle will be measured in anti clockwise direction from the normal (reference). please kindly give me suggestions and if any one has idea on this problem please help me out. My motivation pursuing this problem is to record and reconstruct holograms at different wavelengths. Thanks in advance.

regards

viswanath

posts.post_subject: Mathematical problem of recording and reconstructing images
posts.content_md:
The distance between the fringe planes in holograms (both reflection and transmission) is: d=l*cos(f/2)/(sin(f)=0.5*l/sin(f/2) where l=wavelength and f=angle between object and reference beam.

The distance between the fringes on the surface of the hologram (that is where the fringe planes intersect the surface of the emulsion) is what you see in the holowiki.

The bragg condition for reconstruction is: l/2=d*sin*(f/2)

The angle of the fringe planes intersects the angles of the object and reference beam. So, one could say: fPlane = (fReference+fObject)/2.

All angles measured with respect to the normal of the emulsion.

In these formulas there is no account taken for index of refraction of the emulsion.
